note: Held-out questions target only articles in the held-out family (c-sharp, go, javascript, ruby). 24 answerable + 6 insufficient-evidence. Frozen before the held-out run; not used for tuning.

questions.question: Who originally designed the Go programming language, and in which month and year was Go version 1.0 released?

required_facts.fact: Go was originally designed in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson
Go version 1.0 was released in March 2012

questions.question: Which release of Go first added support for generic programming?

required_facts.fact: Generics were added to Go in version 1.18 (March 15, 2022)

questions.question: If two Go goroutines access shared data without explicit synchronization, is the visibility of writes guaranteed?

required_facts.fact: There are no restrictions on how goroutines access shared data, making data races possible; writes from one goroutine might be partly, entirely, or not at all visible to another with no ordering guarantees

questions.question: In a Go version string such as go1.26.0, what does the second number (26) represent?

required_facts.fact: Go calls the second number in a version the major version, because Go plans to never reach 2.0

questions.question: Who adapted the gopher mascot for Go's open source launch, and who closed the Go! naming dispute issue?

required_facts.fact: Renée French adapted the gopher mascot (introduced in 2009 for the open source launch)
Russ Cox closed the naming dispute issue on October 12, 2010 with the label Unfortunate

questions.question: In which years did the TIOBE index name Go its Programming Language of the Year?

required_facts.fact: Go was named TIOBE Programming Language of the Year in 2009 and again in 2016

questions.question: Who created Node.js, and which corporation holds the JavaScript trademark in the United States?

required_facts.fact: Node.js was created in 2009 by Ryan Dahl
JavaScript is a trademark of Oracle Corporation in the United States

questions.question: What proportion of websites rely on JavaScript for their client-side behavior?

required_facts.fact: 98.9% of all websites use JavaScript as the dominant client-side scripting language

questions.question: Which two restrictions do browser authors use to minimize the risk of malicious JavaScript running on a client computer?

required_facts.fact: Scripts run in a sandbox in which they can only perform Web-related actions
Scripts are constrained by the same-origin policy

questions.question: In JavaScript's type system, is a type associated with a value or with an expression?

required_facts.fact: JavaScript is dynamically typed: a type is associated with a value rather than an expression

questions.question: Which ECMAScript edition first introduced the class keyword into JavaScript?

required_facts.fact: ECMAScript version 6 (released June 2015) introduced the keywords class, extends and super

questions.question: In what year was ECMAScript 6 published, and who originally created JavaScript?

required_facts.fact: ECMAScript 6 was published in 2015
JavaScript was created by Brendan Eich in 1995

questions.question: What did C#'s original name COOL stand for, and which body first approved C# as an international standard?

required_facts.fact: COOL stood for C-like Object Oriented Language
C# was approved as an international standard by Ecma (ECMA-334) in 2002

questions.question: How does a C# program release memory that is no longer needed?

required_facts.fact: Managed memory cannot be explicitly freed; it is automatically garbage collected

questions.question: Can a C# class inherit from multiple base classes?

required_facts.fact: C# does not support multiple inheritance, although a class can implement any number of interfaces

questions.question: Which C# keyword marks the blocks within which memory address pointers may be used?

required_facts.fact: Memory address pointers can only be used within blocks specifically marked as unsafe

questions.question: Does C# have checked exceptions?

required_facts.fact: Checked exceptions are not present in C# (in contrast to Java), a conscious decision based on scalability and version management

questions.question: Since which version does C# offer parametric polymorphism, and what is the name of its unified type system?

required_facts.fact: Since version 2.0, C# offers parametric polymorphism (generics)
The unified type system is called the Common Type System (CTS)

questions.question: Who developed Ruby, and which two names were initially proposed for the language?

required_facts.fact: Ruby development began in the mid-1990s by Yukihiro "Matz" Matsumoto in Japan
The two names initially proposed were Coral and Ruby

questions.question: When was the first public release of Ruby announced?

required_facts.fact: The first public release of Ruby 0.95 was announced on Japanese domestic newsgroups on 21 December 1995

questions.question: What performance goal does the name Ruby 3x3 refer to?

required_facts.fact: Ruby 3x3 signifies that programs would run three times faster in Ruby 3.0 compared to Ruby 2.0

questions.question: Does Ruby support multiple inheritance?

required_facts.fact: Ruby does not support multiple inheritance, though classes can import modules as mixins

questions.question: Starting with which Ruby version has the official Ruby interpreter used the YARV virtual machine?

required_facts.fact: Starting with Ruby 1.9, the official Ruby interpreter has been YARV (Yet Another Ruby VM)

questions.question: Under which two licenses is Ruby distributed effective with Ruby 1.9.3, and what is ZJIT in Ruby 4.0?

required_facts.fact: Effective with Ruby 1.9.3, Ruby is dual-licensed under the Ruby License and the two-clause BSD license
ZJIT is an experimental JIT written in Rust added in Ruby 4.0

questions.question: How many reserved keywords does the C# language define?
questions.missing_detail: The C# article uses the word keyword many times but never counts the reserved keywords. Near-neighbour evidence exists in other articles (Go has 25 keywords, JavaScript 50-60), which makes this plausible but unanswerable from the corpus.

questions.question: How many bytes of stack memory is a new goroutine initially allocated in Go?
questions.missing_detail: The Go article discusses goroutine implementation and multiplexing onto OS threads but never states an initial stack size.

questions.question: What licensing fee does Oracle charge for commercial use of the JavaScript trademark?
questions.missing_detail: The JavaScript article documents the trademark owner and the 2024 letter campaign but never mentions any fee.

questions.question: How many core committers maintain the reference Ruby interpreter?
questions.missing_detail: The Ruby article discusses implementations and maintainership history but never states a committer count.

questions.question: What percentage of GitHub projects use C# as their primary language?
questions.missing_detail: GitHub is mentioned for C# only as the host of standards text development. The corpus records a GitHub popularity claim for JavaScript but none for C#, making this a plausible near-neighbour that the corpus cannot answer.

questions.question: In which Ruby version did pattern matching first become a stable, non-experimental feature?
questions.missing_detail: The Ruby article records pattern matching as experimental in Ruby 2.7.0 but never states a version in which it became stable.
